project.name: Rock Identification App
project.overview: A phone app for hobby rock and mineral collectors. A collector photographs a rock, the app identifies it with a cloud AI model and shows how confident it is, and the collector keeps a personal collection of their finds on the phone. The app must be usable in the field without signal.
scope_in: Rock and mineral identification from a photo
Personal collection of finds, stored on the phone
Use in the field without signal
scope_out: User accounts and cloud sync (first release)
Administrator tools for correcting rock descriptions (later release)

stakeholders.name: Collector
stakeholders.description: Hobby rockhound aged 8 or older who photographs, identifies and collects rocks and minerals, often in the field without signal.
permissions: save finds to their own collection

stakeholders.name: Administrator
stakeholders.description: Maintains the rock descriptions. Planned for a later release.

requirements.title: Identify a rock from a photo
requirements.description: A collector shall be able to take or choose a photo of a rock or mineral and receive the name of the rock or mineral that the identification ranks first.
requirements.source: user input, input.md line 5; clarification round 1

requirements.title: Show identification confidence
requirements.description: The app shall show its confidence in each identification it gives.
requirements.source: user input, input.md line 7; clarification round 1

requirements.title: Save a find to the collection
requirements.description: A collector shall be able to save an identified rock to their collection with its photo, its name and, if location access is allowed, the place where it was found.
requirements.source: user input, input.md lines 9-10; clarification round 1

requirements.title: Save identified rocks to the collection
requirements.description: A collector shall be able to save identified rocks to their personal collection.

requirements.title: Correct rock descriptions
requirements.description: An administrator shall be able to correct wrong rock descriptions in the rock database.
requirements.source: user input, input.md line 18; clarification round 1
requirements.rationale: The user wants this in a later release.

requirements.title: Identify offline photos later
requirements.description: When a photo is taken without an internet connection, the app shall keep it and identify it automatically once a connection is available, without the collector taking the photo again.
requirements.rationale: Settles the conflict between offline use and the cloud model (ISS-001).

requirements.title: Photo sources, formats and size
requirements.description: The app shall accept photos from the camera or the phone's gallery in JPEG, PNG or HEIC format of at most 20 MB, and refuse any other photo with a message that states the allowed formats and size.

requirements.title: Offline use in the field
requirements.description: Taking photos and viewing the collection shall work without an internet connection.
requirements.source: user input, input.md lines 13-14; clarification round 1

requirements.title: Identification accuracy
requirements.rationale: The user wants trustworthy results but does not know a realistic target (ISS-003).

requirements.title: Identification speed
requirements.description: The app shall show an identification result within 5 seconds of the photo being taken when a connection is available.
requirements.source: user input, input.md line 16; clarification round 1
requirements.fit_criterion: 95% of identifications on a 4G connection show a result within 5 seconds of the photo being taken.

requirements.title: Usable by first-time collectors aged 8+
requirements.description: First-time collectors aged 8 or older shall be able to identify a rock and save it to their collection without help.
requirements.source: user input, input.md line 16; clarification round 1
requirements.fit_criterion: In a usability test, at least 8 of 10 first-time users aged 8 or older identify a rock and save it to their collection without help within 2 minutes.

requirements.title: Find locations stay private
requirements.description: The app shall record a find location only after the collector allows location access, and shall never send find locations off the phone.

rules.statement: Identification uses an AI model that runs in the cloud.
Hosting and AI service costs must not exceed 10 EUR per month.
rules.source: user input, input.md line 20; clarification round 1

rules.statement: The collection is stored only on the phone; the first release has no user accounts.
Collectors use a smartphone with a camera.
The app is a mobile app for Android and iOS.

issues.description: NFR-001 said the app works completely offline in the field, but CON-001 says identification runs on an AI model in the cloud, which needs an internet connection. Both cannot hold.
issues.question: In the field without signal, which parts must still work?
issues.suggestion: Taking photos and viewing the collection work offline; photos taken offline are identified automatically once the phone is back online.
issues.resolution: Taking photos and viewing the collection work offline (NFR-001); offline photos are identified automatically later (FR-006).

issues.description: A cloud AI model has running costs, but CON-002 said the owner does not want to pay for servers.
issues.question: What is the most you are willing to pay per month for hosting and the AI service?
issues.suggestion: Use a hosted AI service with a free tier and cap spending at 20 EUR per month.
issues.resolution: Costs are capped at 10 EUR per month (CON-002).

issues.description: 'Accurate' has no measurable target, so nobody can test whether the identification is good enough.
issues.missing_information: An accuracy metric, a target value and the test set.
issues.question: How often must the app name the right rock?
issues.suggestion: The correct name is among the top 3 suggestions for at least 85% of photos in a test set of the 100 most common rocks and minerals.
issues.resolution: The user does not know a realistic target and accepts the risk; the developers set it after testing candidate models.

issues.missing_information: A response-time target and the conditions it applies to.
issues.question: What is the longest acceptable wait for an identification result: 2 s, 5 s or 10 s?
issues.suggestion: 95% of identifications return a result within 5 seconds of taking the photo on a 4G connection.
issues.resolution: Suggestion accepted: 95% of results within 5 seconds on 4G (NFR-003 fit criterion).

issues.description: 'Easy to use, even for kids' named no task, age or success rate.
issues.missing_information: The user group (age), the task and a success rate.
issues.question: From what age must children manage the app without help?
issues.suggestion: In a usability test, at least 8 of 10 first-time users aged 10 or older identify a rock and save it to their collection without help within 2 minutes.
issues.resolution: Suggestion accepted with the age changed to 8 or older (NFR-004 fit criterion).

issues.description: FR-004 repeats FR-003 (input.md lines 9-11 say the same thing twice); FR-003 is the more detailed one.
issues.resolution: FR-004 rejected and merged into FR-003; the user was told in round 1 and did not object.

issues.description: Photo sources, formats and size limits were not stated.
issues.missing_information: Allowed photo sources, file formats and maximum file size.
issues.question: Which photos can be used, and how large may they be?
issues.suggestion: Photos from the camera or the phone's gallery; JPEG, PNG or HEIC; at most 10 MB.
issues.resolution: Camera or gallery; JPEG, PNG or HEIC; at most 20 MB (FR-007).

issues.description: FR-003 stores where a rock was found, which is personal location data, and it was not stated where the collection is kept (on the phone or in an online account).
issues.missing_information: Storage location of the collection, need for accounts, and privacy of find locations.
issues.question: Where is the collection stored, and who may see the find locations?
issues.suggestion: The collection is stored only on the phone, with no user account in the first release; a find location is saved only if the collector allows location access, and it never leaves the phone.

issues.description: The administrator role was mentioned as 'later maybe'; it was unclear whether it belongs to the first release.
issues.question: Is the administrator part of the first release?
issues.suggestion: No; the administrator is planned for a later release.
issues.resolution: The user said the admin can wait for a later version; FR-005 deferred.

issues.description: Nothing says what the app does when it is unsure about an identification.
issues.question: What should the app show when its confidence is low?
issues.suggestion: Below 60% confidence, show the top 3 candidates and say that the result is uncertain.

issues.description: Children may use the app, but no rules for young users are stated.
issues.question: Are there extra rules for young users, such as parental consent before saving find locations?
issues.suggestion: No extra rules in the first release, because there are no accounts and find locations never leave the phone.

issues.description: Because the collection is stored only on the phone (CON-003), it is lost if the phone is lost or replaced.
issues.missing_information: Whether collectors need a backup or export of their collection.
issues.question: Should collectors be able to back up or export their collection?
issues.suggestion: Not in the first release; consider an export of photos and a list of finds in a later release.

user_stories.goal: photograph a rock and see its name and how sure the app is
user_stories.benefit: I can name my finds without asking an expert

user_stories.goal: save a find with its photo, name and the place I found it
user_stories.benefit: I remember what I found and where

user_stories.goal: take photos in the field without signal and get them identified later
user_stories.benefit: I never miss a find just because there is no signal

acceptance_criteria.title: Identify a rock from a camera photo
given: the collector has the camera open in the app
when: they take a photo of a piece of quartz
then: a rock or mineral name is shown within 5 seconds
a confidence value from 0% to 100% is shown next to the name

acceptance_criteria.title: Identify a rock from a gallery photo
given: the phone's gallery contains a 4 MB JPEG photo of a rock
the phone has an internet connection
when: the collector chooses that photo in the app
then: a rock or mineral name and its confidence are shown

acceptance_criteria.title: Photo of exactly 20 MB is accepted
given: the gallery contains a HEIC photo of exactly 20 MB
then: the photo is accepted for identification

acceptance_criteria.title: Photo larger than 20 MB is refused
given: the gallery contains a JPEG photo of 20.1 MB
then: the photo is not sent for identification
the message "Photos must be JPEG, PNG or HEIC and 20 MB or smaller." is shown

acceptance_criteria.title: Unsupported format is refused
given: the gallery contains a 2 MB GIF image
then: the image is not sent for identification
the message "Photos must be JPEG, PNG or HEIC and 20 MB or smaller." is shown

acceptance_criteria.title: Save a find with its location
given: a rock has been identified as quartz
the collector has allowed location access
then: the collection contains a new entry with the photo, the name "quartz" and the current location

acceptance_criteria.title: Save a find without location access
given: a rock has been identified as quartz
the collector has refused location access
then: the collection contains a new entry with the photo and the name "quartz"

acceptance_criteria.title: No location is sent for identification
given: the collector has allowed location access
the camera stores GPS coordinates in its photos
when: a photo is sent to the AI service for identification
then: the data sent contains no GPS coordinates or other location

acceptance_criteria.title: Take a photo and browse the collection without signal
given: the phone has no internet connection
when: the collector takes a photo of a rock
then: the new photo is kept and marked "waiting for identification"
all 3 saved finds are shown with their photos and names

acceptance_criteria.title: Waiting photo is identified when the connection returns
given: one photo is marked "waiting for identification"
when: the phone gets an internet connection
then: the photo is identified without the collector taking it again
its name and confidence are shown and the "waiting for identification" mark is removed

acceptance_criteria.title: Connection lost during identification
given: a waiting photo is being sent for identification
when: the internet connection drops before a result arrives
then: the photo stays marked "waiting for identification"
it is sent again the next time a connection is available

reasons.clarity: One actor, one action and one result.
reasons.completeness: Photo sources and limits are settled in FR-007.
reasons.feasibility: Depends on finding a cloud AI service that identifies rocks within the 10 EUR monthly budget (CON-002).

reasons.clarity: Clear what must be shown and when.
reasons.completeness: Behaviour for low-confidence results is still open (ISS-010).
reasons.feasibility: Identification models return a confidence value with each result.

reasons.clarity: Saved fields and the location condition are stated.
reasons.completeness: Backup or export of the collection is still open (ISS-012).
reasons.feasibility: Local storage of photos and a few fields is standard on phones.

reasons.clarity: "Wrong rock descriptions" does not say who decides what is wrong.
reasons.completeness: Deferred: where the descriptions come from and how corrections reach the app are not defined.
reasons.feasibility: No basis to judge until the source of the rock descriptions is known.

reasons.clarity: Trigger, action and the no-retake condition are explicit.
reasons.completeness: No limit is set on how many waiting photos may be kept.
reasons.feasibility: A local queue with retry on reconnect is a common mobile pattern.

reasons.clarity: Sources, formats, size and refusal behaviour are listed.
reasons.feasibility: Format and size checks are simple to implement.

reasons.clarity: Names exactly which functions work offline.
reasons.completeness: Offline identification is handled by FR-006.
reasons.feasibility: Camera and local storage need no connection.

reasons.clarity: "Accurate" has no metric, so it can be read in many ways.
reasons.completeness: No target or test set; the user accepted leaving it open (ISS-003).
reasons.feasibility: Cannot be judged without a target.

reasons.clarity: Time limit and condition are stated.
reasons.completeness: Fit criterion gives percentile, time and network type.
reasons.feasibility: Upload of photos up to 20 MB over 4G within 5 seconds may require resizing before upload.

reasons.clarity: User group, task and condition are stated.
reasons.completeness: Fit criterion gives sample size, success rate and time limit.
reasons.feasibility: A two-step task is achievable with a simple interface.

reasons.clarity: Two clear conditions on recording and sending location.
reasons.completeness: Covers consent and data leaving the phone, including photo metadata (AC-008).
reasons.feasibility: Location permission and removing GPS data from photos are standard.
